name: Arroyo Seco

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Chardonnay, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon fully without cooking off their freshness.
Chardonnay, Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Pinot Noir is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Summers are close to rainless. Vines need irrigation or deep soil that stores winter rain, but disease is rare.

soil.rock: River deposits are a mix of gravel, sand and silt. They are often fertile, so vines can grow vigorously.
soil.top: The topsoil drains well and still stores water for dry spells, so vines grow evenly. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: Mostly flat. Easy and cheap to farm by machine, but on still nights cold air settles on flat ground, so spring frost is a bigger risk.

winkler: Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.
